description: Guards against the classic failure modes when an agent uses Storywrangler from a SvelteKit app — assuming a dataset instead of discovering the registry, forcing an instrument when the user may just want the data (or reciting a fixed instrument list instead of proposing from the MCP), guessing endpoint params/values instead of using the MCP's docs and registry surfaces, and writing evolving-API SvelteKit code from memory instead of deferring to the Svelte skills.

evals.name: start-from-registry
evals.failure_mode: Agent silently defaults to a corpus (e.g. wikimedia ngrams) and starts wiring, instead of discovering what datasets exist and letting the user choose.
evals.prompt: I want to show some Storywrangler data in my SvelteKit app. Set it up.
expected: Does not assume a dataset — lists the registry with the MCP `list-datasets` first
Surfaces the available datasets to the user and asks which one (keeps the user in the loop)
Uses `get-dataset` to inspect the chosen dataset's dimensions, valid values, and date availability before wiring
Defers the remote-function mechanics to the Svelte skills/MCP rather than re-explaining them

evals.name: data-or-instrument-not-forced
evals.failure_mode: Agent assumes the app must use an instrument (often defaulting to the allotaxonometer) instead of recognising the user may just want the dataset's data, and recites instruments from memory instead of proposing from the MCP.
evals.prompt: I've got the wikimedia ngrams dataset selected. What can I actually build on my page with it?
expected: Does not force an instrument — notes the app can read the dataset's data directly (counts, ranks, time series) or apply an instrument over it
Looks up the available instruments and their use cases in the MCP docs (`get-documentation`) rather than reciting a fixed list
Proposes the options that fit and lets the user choose (user in the loop)
Does not treat top n-grams or term time series as instruments

evals.name: params-from-docs-values-from-registry
evals.failure_mode: Agent guesses endpoint param names, entity id formats, or date formats from memory, conflates the two MCP surfaces, or mishandles the sanitized response.
evals.prompt: Wire the allotaxonometer comparing France and Germany on 2025-01-01 for the wikimedia ngrams dataset.
expected: Gets the endpoint's parameters and response shape from the API reference (`get-documentation api-reference/...`)
Gets the dataset's valid values (entity id scheme, date format, filter dims, date availability) from `get-dataset`
Checks the requested date is available before baking it in, and maps the endpoint's 404 to a real UI state
Handles the sanitized response: non-finite numbers arrive as null or the strings "Infinity"/"-Infinity", so measure fields are possibly-string
Does not guess param names or entity ids from memory

evals.name: defer-sveltekit-code
evals.failure_mode: Agent writes remote-function code from memory against a still-evolving SvelteKit API, instead of deferring the mechanics to the Svelte skills/MCP and contributing only the Storywrangler-specific parts.
evals.prompt: Give me the SvelteKit remote function that calls the storywrangler allotax endpoint.
expected: Defers the remote-function mechanics (file type, query vs prerender, validation, rendering) to the Svelte skills/MCP rather than asserting them from memory
Notes the remote-functions API is still evolving, so the current syntax should come from the Svelte docs/skill
Contributes the Storywrangler-specific parts: the endpoint + params from the API reference, no-auth public read, error-surface mapping
Does not present a full hardcoded remote-function code block as if authoritative
